title: South Coast Summit 2025 - AI-Driven Page Scripting: Practical Use Cases for Dynamics 365
summary: A structured approach to using AI for creating and scaling page scripting test automation in Dynamics 365, progressing through Stand (baseline scripts), Walk (prompt systems), Run (variant generation), and Fly (high-volume PowerShell automation) phases. Covers practical implementation with GitHub Copilot, real-world gotchas, and data governance considerations.
key_points: Page scripting baseline creation provides foundation for AI to understand patterns and generate variants at scale
Using VS Code with GitHub Copilot Pro and Model Context Protocol servers enables multi-file management and integration with Azure DevOps or Jira
Delegating high-volume generation to PowerShell scripts written by AI avoids token limits while leveraging AI's pattern understanding and scripting capabilities
Security considerations include using Azure OpenAI in your own tenant for sensitive data, disabling MFA on test accounts, and validating permissions before batch runs
This approach transfers across multiple ERP systems, working similarly for Business Central and Finance & Operations

quotes.text: AI tools are excellent at understanding patterns and generating structured content, but they're not optimised for very high-volume data operations.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains why delegating high-volume generation to PowerShell is necessary to avoid token limits and inefficiency with direct AI generation

quotes.text: Instead of manually creating script after script, you define your variants in structured files and let the AI generate the complete test suite.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows the efficiency gain when AI handles repetitive script creation after understanding the pattern from baseline examples

quotes.text: The AI won't replace understanding your business processes or knowing how to create good tests. But it absolutely can multiply your ability to execute.
quotes.why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations for AI's role in test automation as an efficiency multiplier rather than a replacement for domain knowledge
